_note: Starter advice for the soil texture model, general guidance written in plain words. Check against a soil science or extension source before relying on it, and fill in source.

texture_loam.signs: Loam: a balanced mix of sand, silt and clay. Crumbly, holds shape loosely when squeezed. Usually the easiest soil to farm.
do_now: Keep it covered with mulch or crop residue between crops.
Avoid tilling when it is wet so it keeps its crumbly structure.
prevent: Add compost each season to keep organic matter up.
Rotate crops and use cover crops.
texture_loam.call_expert_if: Plants grow poorly even though the soil looks good. Get a lab soil test for pH and nutrients.

texture_sand.signs: Sandy: gritty, loose, falls apart when squeezed. Drains fast and dries out quickly; nutrients wash away easily.
do_now: Water more often in smaller amounts, at the base of plants.
prevent: Add compost or manure every season to help it hold water and nutrients.
Split fertilizer into several small doses instead of one big one.
texture_sand.call_expert_if: Leaves turn pale or yellow even with fertilizer. Nutrients may be washing out; get a lab soil test.

texture_clay.signs: Clay: sticky when wet, hard and cracked when dry. Holds water and nutrients well but drains slowly.
do_now: Stay off it and don't till when it is wet.
Water deeply but less often, and check for standing water.
prevent: Add compost to loosen it over time.
Use raised beds or ridges where water collects.
texture_clay.call_expert_if: Water stands for more than a day after rain, or roots look brown and rotten.
